title: Regulated marketplace listing one-pager and acceptance slate
summary: Customer-facing one-pager for regulated marketplace listings plus an internal acceptance slate that groups legal, technical, and product gates for go/no-go decisions in healthcare and finance marketplaces.
body:
OBJECTIVE
This doc serves two purposes: 1) a concise, customer-facing one-pager to use as the marketplace tile or partner sales leave-behind for regulated verticals (healthcare, fintech, government), and 2) an internal acceptance slate/checklist capturing all required artifacts, owners, tests, and signoffs before publishing to a regulated cloud marketplace.

ONE-PAGER (customer-facing)
Title: Redwood Inference — Secure, low-latency LLM inference for regulated apps
Subtitle: Private deployments, enterprise controls, and audit-grade observability for health and financial workloads
Elevator (25–35 words): Run LLM inference with predictable latency and enterprise-grade controls — private VPC deployments, KMS/HSM integrations, and built-in audit logging designed to meet healthcare and finance compliance needs.
Key bullets (tile-friendly):
- Private + hosted deployment options (VPC & on-prem)
- KMS/HSM key management and customer-owned keys
- Audit logs, role-based access, and SSO integrations
- Latency SLOs and canary rollouts for safe model upgrades
- Model/quantization guidance to control cost without sacrificing quality
Call-to-action: Start a secure trial — request a regulated-marketplace sandbox or contact solutions@redwood.example.com
Suggested 1-line tile copy (32–40 chars): "Secure LLM inference for regulated apps"
Suggested 60–90 char subtitle for tile: "Private deployments, KMS, and audit logs for healthcare & finance"
Three short proof points (for tile or detail page):
1) "Validated in HIPAA-ready pilots with two healthcare SaaS partners"
2) "Dedicated GPU pools with SLA-backed latency targets"
3) "Built-in evals and regression alerts tied to prompt suites"

ACCEPTANCE SLATE (internal)
How to use: Each row is a gate. Owner must provide artifact link and signoff. Any unresolved item blocks publish. This slate maps to marketplace publisher requirements + company legal/regulatory baseline.
GATES (high level):
- Legal & Contracts
- Privacy & Data Residency
- Security & Key Management
- Technical Integration / SKU & Billing
- Observability & Telemetry
- UX & Copy Compliance
- Post-publish Monitoring & Rollback Plan

ACCEPTANCE CHECKLIST (compact for quick reviews)
1) Legal & Contracts:
- Required artifact: Marketplace contract addendum and DPA variation for regulated customers
- Owner: Marisol Ortega (Legal ops)
- Acceptance criteria: Signed addendum or template reviewed by counsel; clause list for breach/notification; data processor boundaries clearly stated
- Test: Red-team review of contract language; confirm pricing terms map to publisher expectations

2) Privacy & Data Residency:
- Required artifact: Data residency matrix and privacy FAQ for tile
- Owner: Priya Nair (Privacy)
- Acceptance: Regional deployment options listed; clear guidance on logs retention and deletion windows; PII handling documented
- Test: Deploy sandbox in indicated region; show logs retention controls in console

3) Security & Key Management:
- Required artifact: KMS/HSM integration guide + key rotation policy snippet
- Owner: Alex Gomez (Security)
- Acceptance: Customer-managed key flows documented; HSM compatibility notes included; penetration test summary attached
- Test: End-to-end KMS flow demo in private sandbox; confirm key access logs appear in audit stream

4) Technical Integration / SKU & Billing:
- Required artifact: SKU mapping sheet, trial entitlement rules, API example for marketplace provisioning
- Owner: Riley Chen (GTM eng)
- Acceptance: SKU names match publisher format; trial entitlements automated via API; billing metric (tokens/embedding units) clearly described
- Test: Provision a trial via publisher API; verify metrics show up in billing sandbox and match expected estimates

5) Observability & Telemetry:
- Required artifact: Telemetry contract (events, sample rates, retention) + console screenshots for SLO panels
- Owner: SRE / Observability lead (TBD)
- Acceptance: Token-level cost breakdown available; latency percentiles surfaced; audit logs ingest validated in publisher environment
- Test: Simulate traffic profile; verify dashboards populate and alert rules fire on injected anomalies

6) UX & Copy Compliance:
- Required artifact: Tile assets (logo, 1-line, 60-char subtitle, 250-word detail copy) and accessibility checks
- Owner: Product marketing (TBD)
- Acceptance: Copy avoids making regulated claims (e.g., "HIPAA certified" only allowed if legal-approved); localization snippets for EU/UK language variants included
- Test: Run copy through legal/comms review; verify tile assets pass publisher image spec and accessibility checks

7) Post-publish Monitoring & Rollback Plan:
- Required artifact: Incident playbook for marketplace outages, SKU rollback steps, and customer notification templates
- Owner: SRE + Customer Success (TBD)
- Acceptance: Runbook tested with tabletop exercise; automatic fallback model variant configured for first 48 hours after launch
- Test: Execute simulated incident and confirm rollback script stops traffic and transitions callers to fallback endpoint

ADDITIONAL NOTES (regulatory nuances)
- Healthcare (US): Do not claim "HIPAA compliant" in tile without documented BAA and internal controls; link to BAA request process in tile detail.
- Finance (EU/UK): Ensure data residency and encryption-in-transit & at-rest language matches regulator expectations; flag any market that requires local on-prem deployment.
- Government: Anticipate additional auditing windows and longer approval cycles; include an "on-prem readiness" checklist as part of acceptance.

LAUNCH TIMELINE (recommended minimal runway)
- T-6 weeks: Legal and privacy drafts complete; begin publisher intake
- T-4 weeks: Technical SKU mapping + sandbox provisioning completed
- T-2 weeks: Copy & assets + security tests completed
- T-0: Publish to marketplace; monitor 72-hour burn-in with elevated telemetry sampling

RISK MATRIX (quick)
- High risk: Missing BAA or KMS gaps — block publish
- Medium risk: Minor copy language flagged — acceptable with rapid change window
- Low risk: Localization typos or minor dashboard cosmetic issues — post-launch patch

SAMPLE PUBLISHER NOTES (to copy into intake form)
- Product name: Redwood Inference (Regulated)
- Short description: Enterprise LLM inference with private deployments and audit-grade controls for regulated applications
- Long description (approx 250 words): Redwood Inference provides a unified inference platform for teams that need predictable latency, clear cost controls, and enterprise security for regulated workloads. Choose hosted, dedicated, or private deployments to meet data residency and compliance needs. Integrations include customer-managed KMS support, audit logging, SSO, and per-route observability. Our Optimize toolkit suggests batching and quantization configurations to reduce unit cost while preserving output quality. Redwood offers canary rollouts, rollback policies, and integration support for publisher trial entitlements.
- CTA: Request sandbox

OPEN QUESTIONS / TODOs
- Confirm SRE lead and CS owner for post-publish monitoring
- Finalize BAA template and attach to intake
- Validate images against publisher size limits and accessibility guidelines
- Add sample telemetry event payloads to the telemetry contract artifact

APPENDIX: QUICK CHECKLIST FOR PUBLISHER INTAKE FORM
- [ ] Tile title + 1-line copy
- [ ] 60-char subtitle
- [ ] 250-word product description
- [ ] Logo and hero image (publisher spec compliant)
- [ ] SKU sheet and trial entitlement rules
- [ ] KMS integration guide excerpt
- [ ] Privacy & data residency FAQ
- [ ] Legal contact and BAA process link
- [ ] Console screenshots (SLO, logs, billing metrics)
- [ ] Post-launch incident playbook link

END
